content.body:
Root Declaration

Ethos defines how a player, node, or contributor behaves inside Threshold. It is not morality or rules. It is the behavioral physics of participation: the internal demand loop that determines whether a node stabilizes, drifts, collapses, or ascends.

Ethos acts as the circuit mirror for human behavior inside the system. Whatever passes through the slit - action, contribution, alignment, or neglect - returns as pressure, drift, or anchor. Ethos is where intent becomes force.

Primary Slit

Behavior generates gravity.

Aligned behavior gains orbit stability. Misaligned behavior loses orbit and drifts outward. No behavior collapses inward. This slit allows Ethos to self-assemble.

Branch Behavior

  • Alignment reveals new subnodes.
  • Contribution opens new paths.
  • Stable Presence thickens the branch.

Ethos grows in response to behavior. It is the first branch that reacts to the player.

Node Physics

  • Collapse when behavior contradicts the slit.
  • Drift when behavior is inconsistent.
  • Anchor when behavior is aligned.
  • Resonance when behavior amplifies Flower energy.
  • Pressure when behavior is avoided or neglected.

Ready for Attachment

The slit, triad, and physics make Ethos structurally valid for player contributions, generated subnodes, cross-Flower migration, higher-order principles, spirit-animal alignment, environmental cues, and Fib 5-8 frontier behavior.

Alignment

Measures whether a node's behavior matches the Flower it is orbiting.

  • High alignment strengthens the anchor.
  • Low alignment creates drift.
  • Zero alignment triggers collapse.

Contribution

Tracks whether the node adds energy to the system.

  • Contribution increases orbit height.
  • Non-contribution creates pressure debt.
  • Negative contribution triggers collapse.

Presence

Did you show up?

  • Presence stabilizes orbit.
  • Absence creates drift.
  • Chronic absence triggers migration to the outer halo.
